tax.text: Onder sponsored three Missouri Senate bills from 2020 through 2022 to lower income taxes.
tax.quote: Dr. Onder has repeatedly sponsored legislation to lower income taxes, including SB902 (2022), SB245 (2021), and SB640 (2020).

wages.text: Onder introduced the Worker Enfranchisement Act to change the threshold for certifying a workplace union.
wages.quote: Today, Congressman Bob Onder introduced the Worker Enfranchisement Act, to protect employees from becoming unionized based upon an unfair voting structure.

schools.text: Onder endorsed education savings accounts, charter schools, open enrollment, and homeschooling as alternatives to district-assigned schools.
schools.quote: Policies that put the students' needs first, such as education savings accounts, charter schools, open enrollment, and even homeschooling, continue to face opposition from the left and powerful teacher unions.

safety.text: Onder requested $5 million in federal funding to expand the Jefferson City Police Department headquarters.
safety.quote: Provide a funding level of $5,000,000 for Jefferson City, Missouri’s Police Headquarters Addition as a community project funding request.

immigration.text: Onder sponsored a Missouri law banning sanctuary cities, penalizing public employers and contractors that hire unauthorized immigrants, and ending catch-and-release.
immigration.quote: As a member of the Missouri House, Dr. Onder sponsored and passed HB1549 in 2008 to ban Sanctuary Cities, crack down on public employers and contractors who hire illegal aliens, and end catch-and-release of illegal aliens.

guns.text: Onder helped pass constitutional carry and the Second Amendment Preservation Act and sponsored legislation expanding Castle Doctrine and public-transit carry rights.
guns.quote: Dr. Onder was a leader in the Senate leading to the passage of Constitutional Carry in 2016 and the Second Amendment Preservation Act in 2019.

abortion.text: Onder was a principal author of Missouri's 2019 heartbeat abortion restriction and previously authored abortion-clinic regulations.
abortion.quote: In committee he was a principal author of 2019’s HB 126, the “Heartbeat Bill,” which Missouri Right to Life called the most important pro-life bill in Missouri history.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: Onder says he led citizen groups that helped enact Missouri legislation restricting transgender participation in women's sports.
gender.quote: After leaving the Senate 2023 he led citizen groups in the fight against gender activists, leading to the passage of legislation to protect women’s sports and outlaw harmful transgender hormonal or surgical “treatments” of children.

health.text: Onder opposed expanding Medicaid in Missouri in both 2021 and 2022.
health.quote: Dr. Onder led successful fights against Obamacare Medicaid Expansion in 2021, and against Bidencare Medicaid Expansion in 2022.

voting.text: Onder led negotiations on Missouri's HB1878, opposing expanded early and mail voting and drop boxes while requiring paper ballots.
voting.quote: In 2022, Dr. Onder was the Senate leader in negotiating a package of election reforms, HB1878, that made Missouri’s voting system among the most secure in the nation. In doing so, he thwarted proposals to extend early voting, mail-in voting, and drop boxes. The final bill banned Zuckerbucks and mandated paper ballots.

tax.text: Mann says corporations should pay their fair share in taxes.
tax.quote: Corporations must pay their fair share in taxes.

wages.text: Mann supports the PRO Act, collective bargaining, unions, better wages, and stronger labor-law enforcement.
wages.quote: I support the ProAct so that every worker can collectively bargain for better wages and working conditions, along with strengthening the enforcement capabilities of the National Labor Relations Board.

schools.text: Mann criticizes public funding for private schools and calls for full funding of public education.
schools.quote: Our system is overwhelmed by a lack of resources with private schools receiving public money while public school teachers struggle to make ends meet. Missouri has the resources to expand educational spending but those in power reallocate funding for pet projects while our students and educators fend for themselves.

immigration.text: Mann says asylum seekers should be treated with dignity while also supporting technology to intercept fentanyl.
immigration.quote: She calls for treating asylum seekers with dignity. Mann also says upgraded technology could keep more fentanyl from coming into the United States.

guns.text: Mann supports background checks, safe-storage laws, longer waiting periods for high-capacity weapons, and an assault-weapons ban.
guns.quote: She said she also supports taxing the sale of firearms to generate government revenue, requiring insurance riders on the sale of certain weapons, background checks, extending wait times on the sale of high-capacity weapons and an assault weapons ban.

abortion.text: Mann supports federal protections for abortion access and opposes state and federal abortion bans.
abortion.quote: The United States should set federal standards to prevent extreme laws from restricting access to medical care, so that families do not experience undue financial, geographic, or criminal penalties for protecting their lives and seeking care.

health.text: Mann supports Medicare for All covering medical, mental-health, dental, vision, reproductive, emergency, and prescription care.
health.quote: Medicare for All cuts the ties between healthcare and your job. It allows everyone to receive quality care that is affordable at the hospital, pharmacy, or doctor’s office.

energy.text: Mann supports energy-efficiency initiatives, clean-energy vehicle purchasing, and financial incentives for higher construction energy standards.
energy.quote: We should adopt green initiatives that foster energy efficiency and reduce waste, which will not only create jobs but also save taxpayer dollars.

voting.text: Mann supports mail voting and Election Day voter registration with safeguards.
voting.quote: Voters who are eligible to vote but who did not have an opportunity to register should be able to register and vote on Election Day with proper safeguards

tax.text: Higgins said he would cut government spending and abolish outdated federal agencies, especially the Department of Education.
tax.quote: I would abolish outdated and inefficient federal agencies, in particular the Department of Education. The current congress tried and failed to do this.

debt.text: Higgins proposed letting younger people opt out of Social Security because he said the program was not financially sound.
debt.quote: Let younger citizens opt out. Social Security never was setup to be financially sound.

immigration.text: Higgins said healthy, able-bodied people should be allowed to immigrate to the United States.
immigration.quote: Let any healthy able bodied person immigrate here. Our economy will thrive because of it.

guns.text: Higgins said no gun-ownership restrictions were needed and cited self-defense and deterrence of authoritarian government.
guns.quote: non. Gun ownership provides for defense when police are not near. It also provides a deterrent against an authoritarian take over of our government.

abortion.text: Higgins said abortion should remain a woman's choice during the first two trimesters.
abortion.quote: The first two trimesters. I believe in the woman right to choose.

cannabis.text: Higgins strongly agreed that marijuana should be legalized and regulated similarly to tobacco and alcohol.
cannabis.quote: Marijuana should be legalized and regulated like tobacco and alcohol.

health.text: Higgins advocated using market competition and innovation to make health care affordable and accessible.
health.quote: Let the free market work. Competition and innovation will keep healthcare adequate, affordable and accessible for all.

energy.text: Higgins strongly agreed that domestic oil-exploration and drilling regulations were more restrictive than necessary.
energy.quote: Current regulations on domestic oil exploration and drilling are more restrictive than are necessary.
